15.
The essence of a person's holiness is when he shuts himself within his home and his room, in the aspect of: ‘Go, My people, enter your rooms, etc.’ And it is said: ‘And walk modestly with your G-d.’ This is the aspect of the praise spoken of Torah scholars: ‘All the glory of the king's daughter is within.’ For a person's essential splendor and holiness are when he sits within his home, for it is there that holiness is principally drawn down. Outside, however, is the place where the external forces hold sway. Therefore, it would be fitting for a person to sit within his home always; yet a person is compelled to go outside as well, time and again. This, however, is the aspect of ‘entering and going out.’ For although it would be fitting for a person to cleave to holiness always, in the aspect of ‘entering,’ nevertheless the essential perfection of holiness is precisely when a person merits to be ‘entering and going out.’ For a person must necessarily undergo many ascents and descents every day. When he merits to be proficient in the law—in the aspect of ‘proficient in entering, proficient in going out’—to fulfill what is written: ‘If I ascend to heaven, You are there; and if I make my bed in the netherworld, here You are,’ holding fast to G-d, blessed be He, always with a firm bond, whether in ascent or in descent, then he merits to raise even the places of externality and the lower levels, all of them, into holiness. Then the descent is for the ultimate purpose of ascent.

This is the aspect of the need to leave the house and go outside, time and again. For when he goes outside, which is the aspect of ‘going out,’ since the external forces hold sway there, and remembers G-d, blessed be He, even there and attaches himself to Him, blessed be He, he then refines the places of the external forces and raises everything into holiness. This is the aspect of: ‘When you sit in your house and when you walk on the way’—the aspect of ‘entering and going out.’

This is the aspect of Israel's journey through the wilderness, which is the place of the external forces, a place of snake, fiery serpent and scorpion: to subdue the Other Side and to sift out holiness even from there, in the aspect of: ‘Fortunate is the one who enters and goes out.’ It is precisely then, when they walk in the wilderness, in the places of the external forces, which is the aspect of ‘going out,’ and merit then to find G-d, blessed be He—it is precisely then that G-d, blessed be He, hovers over Israel with very exalted holiness. This is the aspect of the encircling clouds of glory that Israel merited in the wilderness. They are the aspect of a sukkah, the aspect of ‘a mother who shelters her children’: a very exalted holiness that hovers over and shelters a person precisely when he is in the aspect of ‘going out,’ to guard him and rescue him lest he fall there—G-d forbid—forbid!—and helps him subdue the Other Side and sift out holiness precisely from there.

It follows that it is precisely through the aspect of ‘going out’ that one merits a very great ascent, to the aspect of a sukkah. This is the above-mentioned aspect of descent for the ultimate purpose of ascent.

This is the aspect of the commandment of the sukkah, with which G-d, blessed be He, has privileged us at the beginning of the year, at the beginning of repentance, which must be specifically in the aspect of ‘entering and going out.’ We fulfill the aspect of ‘entering’ on Rosh Hashanah, during the Ten Days of Repentance, and on Yom Kippur. Afterward we must also fulfill the aspect of ‘going out’: this is the aspect of [unclear word in supplied Hebrew: תמה]—that one leaves the house to sit in a sukkah—to teach that when a person is in the aspect of ‘going out,’ and seeks and seeks and searches even there to attach himself to G-d, blessed be He, it is precisely then that he merits very exalted holiness, the aspect of a sukkah. This is the aspect of encompassing influences, which guard and protect a person then, when he is in the aspect of ‘going out.’ Through the commandment of the sukkah, we merit throughout the year to undertake, to undertake complete repentance in the aspect of ‘entering and going out.’ Whenever we are in the aspect of ‘going out,’ the shelter of peace then protects us, like a mother who protects her son from falling—G-d forbid—when he walks in a place of danger. This is why we ask specifically at night (which is the aspect of ‘going out,’ in contrast to the quality of daytime): ‘Spread over us the shelter of Your peace.’ For it is precisely then that the shelter of peace protects. For the shelter of peace protects a person always: at every time of danger when protection is needed, then the shelter of peace protects.

This is the aspect of: ‘For He will conceal me in the shelter on a day of trouble.’ It is precisely on a day of trouble, which is the aspect of ‘going out’—that is, at a time when a person falls away from his service, and merits to strengthen himself and not give up hope even then—that the shelter of peace protects us, as explained above.

(Hilchos Rosh Hashanah [Laws of the New Year], Halacha 4, item 7.)

13.
The great virtue of the graves of the Tzaddikim — for there everyone can be repaired. Even one who is between שני הס"מ [opaque source wording: the designation is unresolved; no acronym expansion or two-forces/adversary interpretation is established], G-d forbid — the great Tzadik can extract him from there — when one comes to his holy grave and wishes to return in complete teshuvah. For the death of the great Tzadik is very high and elevated and exalted. And then specifically he intensifies with all his strength to complete what he needs to complete for the benefit of the souls of Israel. For the death of the Tzadik is the aspect of prayer in the aspect of judgment — for the great ba'al ko'ach [master of power] prays — and the sitra achra swallows it. And the prayer — since it is very holy and came from a great ba'al ko'ach — the sitra achra does not have the power to swallow it entirely. Rather, on the contrary — the prayer stands in its throat [b'tzavoroh] — until the sitra achra is compelled through this to vomit and expel and return all the holinesses it has swallowed — including the very essence of its vitality.

And this is the secret of the wondrous repairs and refinements being performed to this day through the death of the ten martyrs [asarah harugei malchus] — as is brought in the sacred writings. And in truth the death of all the Tzaddikim is the aspect of mesiras nefesh [self-sacrifice] for the sanctification of G-d's Name. Especially the death of the Tzaddikim in the diaspora — where all of this is in the manner of the prayer in the aspect of judgment. For they surrender their body to be buried in the diaspora — where the dominion of the sitra achra resides. And it seems to the sitra achra that it is swallowing this holy body. But this holy body is a great ba'al ko'ach and stands in the sitra achra's throat — until it is compelled through this to vomit greatly from within itself and from its belly — until the Tzadik completes what he began. For even during his lifetime he engaged in this all his days and gave his soul for this. But after his passing, he does not stop engaging in this holy service — until he completes everything for the good as he wishes.

And therefore there — upon his holy grave — every person can be repaired. Even the worst of the worst. If he merits to come there during his lifetime and to request and pray there for the repair of his soul. And this too is the matter of the ten Psalms chapters ordained to be said there — see inside.

(Hilchos Chol HaMo'ed, Halacha 4, items 14–15).

In truth — all that G-d, blessed be He, does with a person is all for his benefit. As our Sages of blessed memory said: a person must say: "All that is done from Heaven — is done for good". If so, seemingly it is difficult: why did G-d, blessed be He, command us to pray regarding the affliction, G-d protect us? For all the sufferings and afflictions, G-d forbid, are truly great goodnesses — to cause him to merit through them the life of eternity. But in truth — certainly all that G-d, blessed be He, does with a person is all for the good. And even so, a person must pray and beseech G-d, blessed be He, to emerge from the affliction to spaciousness. For the essential creation of the world was for the sake of the human being who has free will — that everything be delivered into the hands of the person. That is, the person specifically should make vessels and channels to draw down His bounty and kindness, blessed be He, below. And without the repair of the vessels — made by the person — the flow of kindness cannot descend below. For if the kindness were to descend before the repair of the vessels — it would be in the aspect of: "an abundance of oil causes the lamp to be extinguished." And then the kindness would be transformed into severe judgment, G-d forbid.

And the essential repair of the vessels is through Torah and prayer. And primarily through prayer. And therefore before a person prays — certainly everything that comes upon him is a great goodness, even sufferings, G-d forbid. For everything is for his benefit. For according to his deeds — no flow and vitality can descend to him except through this. And even this comes in great kindness. For if only kindness without any judgment at all were to flow to him — it would be, G-d forbid, in the aspect of an abundance of light that damages more. Therefore the essential repair is through prayer. For through prayer one sweetens the judgments and repairs vessels — in a manner that one can receive the flow of His blessed kindness without sufferings. Only through the repairs of the vessels that he repaired through prayer. And therefore the essential repair of prayer is through gazing at the purpose and including all the prayer in the One — where it is entirely good. As explained in the main text. For without this — one cannot pray at all because of the aforementioned difficulty. As our Sages of blessed memory posed: "But does one give a child whatever he wants?" For since G-d, blessed be He, knows the truth — that these sufferings from deficiency of livelihood and the like are for his eternal benefit — how will G-d, blessed be He, hear his prayer to give him what he asks and thereby cause him eternal harm, G-d forbid? As in what is written: "There is wealth kept for its owner to his detriment". And as is brought in the holy Zohar: "חיכת בהון בעותרא בהאי עלמא ולבתר קטילת לון" — "She toys with them through wealth in this world, and afterward kills them." G-d forbid.

And therefore in truth the essential repair of prayer is through gazing at the true purpose in truth — and knowing and believing that everything is for the good. And then specifically one can pray afterwards for all that he needs. For then he can draw repairs from the light of the impression of the nullification toward the purpose — through which vessels will be made to draw through them His blessed abundant bounty and kindness in perfection with no lack of anything: livelihood and wealth and health — and health — children, life, and sustenance. And even so — no harm and loss whatsoever will come to him through this, G-d forbid, in any direction — neither in this world nor in the World to Come. Rather, everything will be for eternal good as well. Since he has already repaired the vessels properly to receive through them the flow of kindness.

And therefore in truth no person knows how to pray in perfection — except the truly righteous Tzaddikim. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "One who has a sick person in his house — let him go to a sage and ask him to pray for mercy on the sick person's behalf." And other people must bind their prayer to the Tzaddikim aforementioned — and they will elevate their prayer as is proper — to draw for them the flow of what they need: children, life, and sustenance, etc. In a manner that it will not harm them eternally, G-d forbid. Rather, on the contrary — through the flow specifically they will be repaired and return to G-d.

And therefore in truth there are many wonders and hidden matters in this matter of prayer. And therefore in truth it is forbidden to be stubborn and to press oneself about anything in one's prayer — as is explained elsewhere. For perhaps in truth it is impossible to fulfill one's request even through prayer — as it may harm him more, G-d forbid, if his request is fulfilled. And if he presses and is very stubborn in his prayer — it could be that he will accomplish with G-d, blessed be He, the fulfillment of his request. For a person has great power to accomplish through his prayer. But it will not be for his benefit, G-d forbid. For he has not yet merited through his prayer to repair the vessel in perfection that is needed for receiving the flow that he wants. It is thus found: that as long as he is not praying for his needs — all the lacks he has are a great goodness for him. But through prayer he repairs vessels properly — through which he can — [can] — receive the flow of kindness to fill all the lacks — and it will not — [not] — harm him at all eternally either. And all of this — through gazing in truth at the purpose — which is entirely good as above.

And therefore in truth the essential prayer must truly be for one's eternal purpose. And this is the aspect of what is brought in the sacred books: that the essential prayer must be for the sake of making good the lack of the Shechinah, as it were. And therefore even the prayer one prays for one's physical needs — one should pray that G-d, blessed be He, give him all his needs in a manner that will bring him eternal success. And this is the aspect of the order of the Shemoneh Esreh that our Sages of blessed memory arranged for us. And we begin first with the praise of the Omnipresent — in the first three blessings. And in the first blessing we mention how He, blessed be He, bestows good kindnesses — and all that He does is entirely for the good. And He is the King, helper, savior, and shield. And afterwards in the blessing of "Who revives the dead" — one includes also other salvations and sustenance and healing. And one includes them many times together with the matter of the revival of the dead. That is, we praise and give thanks to G-d, blessed be He, that all that He does with us is for our eternal benefit — which is the aspect of the revival of the dead. And only for this does He cause wondrous salvations to sprout for us at all times also in the physical: in matters of sustenance and healing and the like. All in a manner that will bring eternal success — also after the Revival. And thus it is understood that also the fact that the flow is sometimes delayed, G-d forbid — all of it is for our eternal benefit after the Revival. For since G-d, blessed be He, is so good and so beneficent and so all-powerful — and does kindness with the entire world at all times — sustains the living, etc. — if so, from where does it come that sometimes the flow is delayed? Certainly one must believe that it is only for eternal benefit. And therefore there the blessing mentions the matter of the Revival of the Dead many times in close proximity to the matter of sustenance. For in the matter of sustenance, a person's heart becomes most distorted — and he finds the delay in livelihood difficult every time. And therefore one must especially be reminded in this matter — that all the sustenance and provision that G-d, blessed be He, provides for a person — all of it is for his eternal benefit after the Revival of the Dead. And for this very same reason the sustenance is sometimes delayed — for his eternal benefit.

And afterwards one says Kedushah and the blessing "You are holy" — which is the aspect of the very essence of the purpose: that all of Israel should merit after the Revival to sanctify His blessed Name together with all the holy ones who will praise You forever. And after having arranged the praise of the Omnipresent and proclaimed that all that G-d, blessed be He, does is entirely for the good — then one prays for his needs. And even here one first prays chiefly for the ultimate purpose: for knowledge and repentance and forgiveness of sin. And then one prays for the needs of the body. But all our intention even in this is only for the eternal purpose. For we know and acknowledge that G-d, blessed be He, is all-powerful — and all that He does with us is entirely for the good. Only even so it is His blessed will that we pray before Him for our needs — in order to make vessels to receive the flow in perfection. And the essential thing — only for the sake of the eternal purpose. And therefore we recite the Kriyas Shma before the prayer. For through the Kriyas Shma we are encompassed in the One. And then specifically one can pray — as mentioned above.

In truth — all that G-d, blessed be He, does with a person is all for his benefit. As our Sages of blessed memory said: a person must say: "All that is done from Heaven — is done for good". If so, seemingly it is difficult: why did G-d, blessed be He, command us to pray regarding the affliction, G-d protect us? For all the sufferings and afflictions, G-d forbid, are truly great goodnesses — to cause him to merit through them the life of eternity. But in truth — certainly all that G-d, blessed be He, does with a person is all for the good. And even so, a person must pray and beseech G-d, blessed be He, to emerge from the affliction to spaciousness. For the essential creation of the world was for the sake of the human being who has free will — that everything be delivered into the hands of the person. That is, the person specifically should make vessels and channels to draw down His bounty and kindness, blessed be He, below. And without the repair of the vessels — made by the person — the flow of kindness cannot descend below. For if the kindness were to descend before the repair of the vessels — it would be in the aspect of: "an abundance of oil causes the lamp to be extinguished." And then the kindness would be transformed into severe judgment, G-d forbid.

And the essential repair of the vessels is through Torah and prayer. And primarily through prayer. And therefore before a person prays — certainly everything that comes upon him is a great goodness, even sufferings, G-d forbid. For everything is for his benefit. For according to his deeds — no flow and vitality can descend to him except through this. And even this comes in great kindness. For if only kindness without any judgment at all were to flow to him — it would be, G-d forbid, in the aspect of an abundance of light that damages more. Therefore the essential repair is through prayer. For through prayer one sweetens the judgments and repairs vessels — in a manner that one can receive the flow of His blessed kindness without sufferings. Only through the repairs of the vessels that he repaired through prayer. And therefore the essential repair of prayer is through gazing at the purpose and including all the prayer in the One — where it is entirely good. As explained in the main text. For without this — one cannot pray at all because of the aforementioned difficulty. As our Sages of blessed memory posed: "But does one give a child whatever he wants?" For since G-d, blessed be He, knows the truth — that these sufferings from deficiency of livelihood and the like are for his eternal benefit — how will G-d, blessed be He, hear his prayer to give him what he asks and thereby cause him eternal harm, G-d forbid? As in what is written: "There is wealth kept for its owner to his detriment". And as is brought in the holy Zohar: "חיכת בהון בעותרא בהאי עלמא ולבתר קטילת לון" — "She toys with them through wealth in this world, and afterward kills them." G-d forbid.

And therefore in truth the essential repair of prayer is through gazing at the true purpose in truth — and knowing and believing that everything is for the good. And then specifically one can pray afterwards for all that he needs. For then he can draw repairs from the light of the impression of the nullification toward the purpose — through which vessels will be made to draw through them His blessed abundant bounty and kindness in perfection with no lack of anything: livelihood and wealth and health — and health — children, life, and sustenance. And even so — no harm and loss whatsoever will come to him through this, G-d forbid, in any direction — neither in this world nor in the World to Come. Rather, everything will be for eternal good as well. Since he has already repaired the vessels properly to receive through them the flow of kindness.

And therefore in truth no person knows how to pray in perfection — except the truly righteous Tzaddikim. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "One who has a sick person in his house — let him go to a sage and ask him to pray for mercy on the sick person's behalf." And other people must bind their prayer to the Tzaddikim aforementioned — and they will elevate their prayer as is proper — to draw for them the flow of what they need: children, life, and sustenance, etc. In a manner that it will not harm them eternally, G-d forbid. Rather, on the contrary — through the flow specifically they will be repaired and return to G-d.

And therefore in truth there are many wonders and hidden matters in this matter of prayer. And therefore in truth it is forbidden to be stubborn and to press oneself about anything in one's prayer — as is explained elsewhere. For perhaps in truth it is impossible to fulfill one's request even through prayer — as it may harm him more, G-d forbid, if his request is fulfilled. And if he presses and is very stubborn in his prayer — it could be that he will accomplish with G-d, blessed be He, the fulfillment of his request. For a person has great power to accomplish through his prayer. But it will not be for his benefit, G-d forbid. For he has not yet merited through his prayer to repair the vessel in perfection that is needed for receiving the flow that he wants. It is thus found: that as long as he is not praying for his needs — all the lacks he has are a great goodness for him. But through prayer he repairs vessels properly — through which he can — [can] — receive the flow of kindness to fill all the lacks — and it will not — [not] — harm him at all eternally either. And all of this — through gazing in truth at the purpose — which is entirely good as above.

And therefore in truth the essential prayer must truly be for one's eternal purpose. And this is the aspect of what is brought in the sacred books: that the essential prayer must be for the sake of making good the lack of the Shechinah, as it were. And therefore even the prayer one prays for one's physical needs — one should pray that G-d, blessed be He, give him all his needs in a manner that will bring him eternal success. And this is the aspect of the order of the Shemoneh Esreh that our Sages of blessed memory arranged for us. And we begin first with the praise of the Omnipresent — in the first three blessings. And in the first blessing we mention how He, blessed be He, bestows good kindnesses — and all that He does is entirely for the good. And He is the King, helper, savior, and shield. And afterwards in the blessing of "Who revives the dead" — one includes also other salvations and sustenance and healing. And one includes them many times together with the matter of the revival of the dead. That is, we praise and give thanks to G-d, blessed be He, that all that He does with us is for our eternal benefit — which is the aspect of the revival of the dead. And only for this does He cause wondrous salvations to sprout for us at all times also in the physical: in matters of sustenance and healing and the like. operations.before:
All the days of the year one must prepare himself for Rosh Hashanah — which is the Day of Judgment. For the essential thing is Rosh Hashanah. For just as a person must prepare himself all the days of his life for the great and awesome Day of Judgment in the future — likewise in the particular, he must prepare himself all the days of the year for Rosh Hashanah — which is the Day of Judgment. For it is awesome and dreadful, etc. And especially one must begin and prepare himself when he sees the days approaching — which is from the fifteenth of Av onwards. For then begins the sweetening of the sin of the Golden Calf and the sin of the Spies — through which, in all of this, the holy memory [zikaron d'kedushah] was blemished. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "From the day the Tablets were broken, forgetting descended upon the world." And on the fifteenth of Av began the sweetening of the breaking of the Tablets — and the illumination of the forty days of favor begins to shine. For then they subsequently received on Yom Kippur the second Tablets — which merited the aspect of the repair of memory. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory said: "No days were as good for Israel as the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur." For on the fifteenth of Av begins to shine the illumination from the second Tablets given on Yom Kippur. And therefore on the fifteenth of Av the sin of the Spies was also repaired — for on it the desert generation ceased dying, as our Sages of blessed memory said. And therefore from the fifteenth of Av one must begin to rise at midnight — which is the aspect of the repair of memory.

And afterwards during the month of Elul one engages in this more and more. And all of Israel is awakened then and remembers G-d, blessed be He, and the World to Come. And this is the aspect of the blowing of the shofar throughout the month of Elul. For the shofar is the aspect of remembrance — as it is written: "And it shall be for you a remembrance". And the essential repair of memory flows on Rosh Hashanah — when the essential commandment of the shofar is performed. Which is the Day of Remembrance [yom hazikaron]. For it is the first of the Ten Days of Repentance — and one must draw upon himself the aforementioned remembrance. Through which comes the essential teshuvah. And for this purpose one must journey to the Tzaddikim for Rosh Hashanah. For this is the essential occupation of the Tzaddikim always — to remind us of our eternal purpose in the World to Come, and to teach us counsels and straight paths to merit this. And especially the Tzaddikim engage in this on Rosh Hashanah, as explained within [the cited work].

And this remembrance is in the general and in the particular. And this is the secret of sleep and awakening from sleep at Rosh Hashanah. For sleep is the aspect of remembrance of the World to Come in the general — for then the soul ascends to the aspect of the World to Come. And afterwards — upon awakening from sleep — then one must engage in this in the particular. And afterwards — on Yom Kippur — then comes the completion of the repair of the remembrance. And therefore the second Tablets were given then. And the High Priest entered on it into the innermost chamber, as explained within [the cited work].

And afterwards one enters the sukkah — which is the encompassing clouds of glory [ananei kavod] that protect us so that the evil eye no longer has dominion over us — which is the aspect of the husk of Amalek. So as not to blemish again, G-d forbid, the holy memory we drew upon ourselves in these days — especially on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur. And this is the aspect of the joy one multiplies on Sukkos — in order to repair also through this the aspect of — [the aspect of] — the imagination [hamedameh]. For all of this is the aspect of the repair of memory aforementioned. And therefore one then takes the four species of the lulav. And the holy Zohar explains that through this we take Him, blessed be He, as it were, in our hands — that is, we draw upon ourselves the remembrance in the particular: which is the aspect of the hints whereby G-d, blessed be He, contracts Himself from the Infinite to the infinite [me'ain sof ad ain techlis] in thought, speech, and action each day — and hints to the person everywhere and at all times to draw close to Him. Which is the aspect of the wavings that are waved to all directions. That is, we draw upon ourselves these hints aforementioned.

(Hilchos Bircas HaRe'iyah, Halacha 5, items 17, 19.)

operations.before: The reading "sleep" for השנה follows the sentence about the soul’s ascent and awakening; it does not supply Hebrew pointing or emend the text. Every single person of Israel — in the inner depth of his soul — yearns and burns very greatly for G-d, blessed be He. Because in the inner depth he gazes at all times toward the purpose [tachlis] — which is the light of the Infinite [ohr ha'ain sof] — from which his root derives. And he wishes to cleave and be encompassed there. But since this aspect is in the aspect of ratzo v'shov [advance and retreat] — and when he is in the aspect of shov [retreat], then the vessels of the expanded consciousness [kailim d'hamoi'ach] — which are the aspect of the garments — are unable to receive the light of the shining from there. And then most often the light of the impression [reshimah] of the nullification [bitul] is entirely forgotten by him. And through the commandment of tzitzis — the garments are repaired. Which are the aspect of — [the aspect of] — the vessels of the expanded consciousness. So that they can receive the light of the shining of the impression from the nullification — from which is the root of all Torah. And this is the aspect of: "And you shall see it, etc." — whose essential [reference] is to the techeiles [blue dye] in the tzitzis. That is, one must look and gaze greatly upon the purpose [tachlis] — which is the aspect of techeiles — as explained in the inner teachings. And this: "and you shall not go astray after your hearts and after your eyes" — that he should close his eyes from the sight of this world entirely and direct his vision and his withdrawal only toward the ultimate purpose alone. "So that you shall remember and do all My commandments". For through the commandment of tzitzis one merits to well remember the light of the impression aforementioned — from which flows the totality of Torah and commandments.

(Hilchos Netilas Yodayim Shacharis, Halacha 4, item 8).
